conventions.convention: Macroscopic S_c is defined on equilibrium macrostates; Boltzmann entropy is defined on nonempty macrocells, Gibbs–Shannon entropy on probability vectors, and von Neumann entropy on the supplier's finite-sector density operators. No identification among these quantities is adopted.
Logarithms are natural and have positive arguments. Empty macrocells are excluded, and p_i log p_i is defined as zero when p_i=0. Physical entropy has units J K⁻¹.

Trajectory observables require a specified path probability law and measurability; finite expectation requires integrability. A positive ensemble mean does not imply a nonnegative value in every realization.

Continuum fields use an open spatial region in R³, a nonempty open time interval, metre and second coordinates, and C¹ local-state components. Physical coordinate i corresponds to library function coordinate i−1. Local equilibrium is a stipulated map q applied pointwise to the local parameters.

Fourier transport is a conditional constitutive choice j_Q=−K∇T; isotropic K=κI₃ has κ≥0. Conductivity has units W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ and heat-energy flux has units W m⁻². Matrix display indices are one-based translations of the supplier's zero-based indices.

Unitary entropy invariance uses exactly the published closed finite-sector model, its adopted normalized canonical preparation, and both Countable Choice and Choice. It asserts neither an infinite-dimensional entropy result nor equilibration.

Observations, derived estimates, model predictions, and statistical comparisons are separate records. Missing source details remain omissions; agreement does not prove a postulate, and empirical premises retain their qualifications.

load_bearing.statement: These are distinct definitions on different domains: S_c acts on an equilibrium macrostate, S_B on a chosen macrocell, S_G on a specified probability vector, and S_vN on a finite-sector density operator. No identification or sampling rule is supplied.

A local-equilibrium approximation is a model-declared map q: Z→E_eq, together with the assumption that the state assigned at (x,t) is q(z(x,t)). Initial data, boundary conditions, conservation equations, constitutive assumptions and empirical scope must be supplied before an evolution or transport conclusion.

A Fourier heat-transport model may postulate j_Q(x,t)=−K(x,t)∇T(x,t). These are constitutive choices for specified material, geometry, regime, field regularity and boundary conditions; equilibrium entropy postulates and dimensional consistency alone do not determine the coefficients.

The macroscopic second-law postulate compares specified equilibrium endpoints and does not assert that every microscopic realization has nonnegative entropy change. Positivity of an ensemble mean does not imply positivity in every realization.

An empirical claim must identify its source, preparation, apparatus, calibration, sampling, uncertainty and limitations; observations, estimates, predictions and statistical comparisons must remain separate.

Under exactly the named published finite-sector supplier's model and choice assumptions, every declared preparation and every real t satisfy S_vN(ρ(t))=S_vN(ρ(0)); the adopted canonical preparation is stationary; and a different preparation is never mapped to it by this unitary flow.

concerns.concern: The Example writes “Z=(0,∞)⊆R¹” and gives z a scalar formula, whereas the cited Euclidean-space definition makes R¹ the space of functions {0}→R. A1 subsequently writes Z⊆R. The intended canonical identification of a scalar with its one-coordinate vector is immediate, but should be stated so the range declaration and q have consistent types.

seams_checked.note: The actual finite-microstate supplier defines a finite nonempty Ω and numerical energy map ε, with physical E=ε J and separately supplied mechanical interpretation. The consuming entropy definition preserves this interface and explicitly adopts no sampling rule or macroscopic identification. Both page summaries preserve the distinction between conditional statistical preparations and equilibration; the supplier page makes no reverse claim requiring the irreversible-boundaries results.
